description: The chart illustrates model “effect” values across language families for several multilingual BERT-based model variants, shown as grouped bars with error bars. The category axis is horizontal and labeled “family,” with families arranged left to right as IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic (additional families may be present but are not fully visible at the left edge of the image); the value axis is vertical and labeled “effect,” using a linear scale with visible tick marks at approximately 10, 20, and 30 (the plotted range extends slightly above 30). Each family has a cluster of four bars corresponding to the legend entries mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light pink), and XLM-B2 (red), with vertical black error bars on each bar. Approximate bar heights by family are: IE-Romance shows light pink around the mid-to-high 20s and red around the mid-20s, while the green bars are lower (roughly around the low teens to mid-teens); IE-Slavic shows the green bars as the tallest in that cluster (both around the low-to-mid 30s), with light pink and red also high (around the low-to-mid 30s); IE-other shows blue-toned bars present in the plot area (not listed in the visible legend) around the low-to-mid 20s, with the green bars near the high teens/around 20 and the red/pink bars around the mid-to-high 20s; Isolate shows small bars near the baseline (roughly around 1–3) for the green and red/pink series; Semitic shows the tallest bars in the visible portion, with blue-toned bars around the low-to-mid 30s and red/pink bars reaching the mid-to-high 30s, while the green bars are much shorter (around a few units); Uralic shows very small bars near the baseline (roughly around 1–3) across the visible series. The bars within each family are positioned side-by-side (not stacked), and no explicit sorting by magnitude is indicated beyond the fixed left-to-right family order; no bars appear specially highlighted beyond the consistent color coding and the presence of error bars.
